# quietsend

> Send Solana devnet USDC with only a NEAR account, via NEAR Chain Signatures.
> The contribution is not the sending: it is the guard that inspects and
> simulates a Solana transaction before a NEAR account is asked to sign it.

NEAR testnet and Solana devnet only. Devnet USDC has no value. Not audited.

## What an agent should know first

Chain Signatures sign whatever bytes they are handed. In hide-recipient mode
those bytes are built by a third party (MagicBlock's API), so the transaction
builder is untrusted by design. Before any signature exists, the transaction is
parsed and simulated and refused unless it is exactly what was requested.

A NEAR function-call access key CANNOT attach a deposit, and `sign` requires
1 yoctoNEAR. An agent holding a function-call key therefore cannot reach the
signer at all. Every send needs a full-access key, which in the web app means a
human approving in their wallet. There is no spending-limit system and no MCP
server in this repo; do not expect either.

## Docs

- [Integrating](/docs/INTEGRATING.md): the one function and one interface an
  agent or Node process calls, with a working non-browser wallet implementation.
- [Security model](/docs/SECURITY.md): what the guard does and does not protect
  against. The guard is input validation, not a security boundary — it runs in
  the page that requests the signature.
- [README](/docs/README.md): what it is, with a command proving every claim.
- [Where this goes next](/docs/next-version.md): the on-chain guard, and what
  was evaluated and rejected.

## Verify rather than trust

- `npm test` — 44 offline tests, under a second, no network or wallet. Twelve
  hostile transactions, each refused with a named reason.
- `npx tsx web/scripts/verify-lib.ts` — read-only run against live devnet, no
  credentials: derivation cross-checked two ways, a real overcharge refused,
  payout matching exercised.
- `#/demo` in the running app — the same twelve attacks in the browser, with a
  toggle showing what a client without the guard would sign.

## Limits worth stating plainly

Hide-recipient mode breaks the direct sender-to-recipient link on Solana. It
does NOT hide amounts or timing, and the NEAR sign call is public in both modes.
Unlinking depends on MagicBlock and Intel TDX, not on a proof.
